title: LOGO DISPLAY ISSUE IN 3D TAB
content:
![c42c537d41a5455ea8e58db76dbf243e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202508/edba58eaead0408d8368b5446faceebf/images/c42c537d41a5455ea8e58db76dbf243eScreenshot%202025-08-09%20125212.jpg)when i download that file from closet connect offical and open in clo 3d the logo is showing in 2d tab in pattern but not showing in 3d tab ? can some one tell me how logo show in t-shirt in 3d tab

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hellow - Check Placement:Click on Graphic , On the Property editor , Graphic Configuration you will see FACE . Be sure put it in FRONT Sometimes it’s on the wrong side of the fabric and you just can’t see it in 3D.- Opacity Issue:Select the fabric where the graphic is applied → In Property Editor, check Texture Map slots. If the fabric has an Opacity Map or Graphic Opacity set to 0%, the logo will be invisible in 3D.And know that sometimes when you download an asset from CLO-SET, sometimes the graphic isn’t embedded—it’s just a reference link. Right-click the graphic → Change Graphic → Re-import the image file manually.

Comment 2: Hi There. Looks like you may have installed an unofficial version of CLO. We would first recommend subscribing and downloading CLO directly from our website. This will likely solve many issues and allow you to update to CLO 2025
content_description: This web page aims to provide guidance on how to display logos in 3D on T-shirts within CLO 3D after downloading from Closet Connect.

title: Do you know how to get rid of back swelling?
content:
![5080bc687b1947fb82c02bccc1cf5b7c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202508/d4ced58b2b3849d5945c9ae5bd8ec7af/images/5080bc687b1947fb82c02bccc1cf5b7c%E3%82%B9%E3%82%AF%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A7%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%202025-08-07%2018.44.22.png)As you can see from the attached jacket, the back of the jacket is floating up, and when I set the animation, pressure is applied, causing the jacket to rise up. What can I do to prevent this back from floating up? I'm not a fashion student, so I don't know why this happens, so I'd appreciate your help!

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: If you sew a jacket or coat and the back keeps riding up toward the neck, it’s usually a pattern balance or back length issue.SO If the center back length is shorter than needed compared to the body or front, the garment will pull up in the back.Fix: Add length to the back pattern between the waistline and shoulder (about 1–2 cm or more as needed).And sometimes If the back width is too narrow, or the back armhole is too tight, the garment will ride up when you move your arms.

Comment 3: Thank you for your comment! The floating during animation is gone!! Sorry for my poor explanation. The floating itself was fixed by applying pressure and changing to Animation Stable, but the fabric is still gathering in the back area, causing wrinkles. Therefore, I would like to eliminate this gathering of fabric.The current back pattern is as follows:

Comment 4: There may not be enough information here. When you say pressure is applied did you apply pressure to the pattern piece? If so this should be removed.When you go to animation mode have you made sure that you have change the simulation type to Animation Stable?
content_description: This webpage aims to provide solutions and guidance for preventing the back of jackets from floating up during animation or wear, particularly for those unfamiliar with fashion design principles.

title: Bloom & Breeze – Fashion in the Fields 🌸🌿
content:
🌸✨ There’s something magical about watching clothes dance in the breeze. For this piece, I wanted to capture that in-between moment – when garments aren’t on the runway yet, but are already alive. Each piece was digitally crafted in CLO3D, then placed in a sunny daisy field where nature takes over as the ultimate stylist.  
It’s a reminder that fashion doesn’t just live on bodies – it lives in the air, in the light, and in the stories we imagine while it moves.

title: How To Lay The Pattern On The Bias Of The Fabric And Cut On Clo3D?
content:
How To Lay The Pattern On The Bias And Cut On Clo3D?

Can we set grain line on the fabric?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Sorry. I forgot to mention. The purpose I want to set the grainline here is not visual purposes.I want to lay the neck band of a T-shirt on the bias of the fabric.I want to use the bias stretch ratio, you know. I think you showed how to set grainline for "visual purposes"So with your method can It simulates "the bias stretch ratio" for the neck band of a T-shirt?
Reply 1: Hi! Have you tried the method? If you change the grainline as explained below for a pattern piece, it changes the drape of the fabric, not just the print or texture. You can see the drape change when simulating back to back. Rotating the maps is done with the black flat gizmo in the upper right corner with the same tool.

Comment 2: I watched thisYouTube Series completely by taking notes.I don't remember that I got the answer of this question. Maybe I missed.So can you answer me please? Thanks.
Reply 1: Hi, with the Edit Texture tool, you either click on the pattern piece to activate the grainline, then click and drag on the grainline sign to rotate it freehand (a precision window will pop up if you right-click at the same time as you are dragging), or you select the pattern piece with Transform Pattern and change the grainline numerically in the Property Editor.

Comment 3: We would also add that many questions can be asked to the new CLO chatbot on the CLO help center which will often answer CLO foundational questions faster than we can 🙂https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/31fc9acecaac4831a13dd8d5608d65e9
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on laying patterns on the bias and cutting fabric in Clo3D, including instructions on setting the grain line.

title: How To Add Shrinkage Ratio To The Fabric?
content:
How To Add Shrinkage Ratio To The Fabric?

(The shrink ratio when you wash the fabric.)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Then I assume I deal this issue with this way. Right? Can you check this method? Is It the right way?Step 1) I draft the pattern and simulate on Clo3D.Step 2) I measure the actual fabric’s elasticity amount.I compensate the elasticity by increasing the regarding measures on the 2D Screen on the Clo3DHowever I do not simulate after do It.Because the clothes appear loose and may even slip off the avatar.If I want to simulate It again I copy the pattern on the Step 1 and simulate that.Am I right?
Reply 1: Hi There. Please remember that unless you reply to a previous reply no one will see the alert about a new question in an old post. It is often best to make a new post for a questions. You should also always try and add images of your 2D and 3D windows so the moderators have a better idea of what you are talking aboutStep 1 - correct.Step 2 - For fabric you should be using the CLO FAB Fabric creator. Putting in the correct fabric composition to make a digital version of your real world fabric.Unless you are actually using elastic tapes in the real world garment then you should not be worrying about this.If you use the correct fabric made in CLO fab and have the correct sized avatar and have patterned properly then you should be fine. But if you pattern keeps falling off then your pattern is clearly too big and should be adjusted and edited in 2D

Comment 2: Thank you very much.

Comment 3: I want to compensate the shrinkage amount in the fabric by modifying the pattern.Even the free sewing pattern drafting software can do this. Seamly2D.How can I do this with the methods you mentioned?“If you want to change the pattern in 2D you would use the Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools to edit and scale”Let’s say the shrinkage ratios are like these;Warp : 4%Weft : 6%Bias : 3%?
Reply 1: (Hi there, just a note on the interface here - if you do not reply directly under one of our comments, we will unfortunately not get a notification that there has been a new message and not see it, or only with delay.) https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/05ccb76a36b348db8c7ab859c9aace8a It is shown here how to resize patterns in all directions. There is a precision window that can be triggered with a click sequence of your mouse. Then, you could add the percentages into it. E.g. if the shrinkage is 4%, you would resize the pattern to 96% along that direction.

Comment 4: So you said It's 3D-only.How do I apply the Shrinkage effect on the 2D pattern?
Reply 1: Applying shrinkage is the exact same as Melody has already answered you within the pattern piece Property Editor. Here is an article also available on our website https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/05ccb76a36b348db8c7ab859c9aace8a is something that would not be applied in 2D. shrinkage refers to the process of adjusting a pattern's size and shape to simulate the effects of fabric shrinkage, often due to washing or other treatments post cutting.If you want to change the pattern in 2D you would use the Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools to edit and scale

Comment 5: Question 1) Is This setting you showed is only visual purposes?Or It is literally shrink the pattern you draft?Question 2) Can I set on and off this shrinkage setting? Or create shrinkage presets?For example I can create same pattern with different shrinkage ratio presets?Question 3) Can I create Stretch presets?For example I can create same pattern with different stretch ratio presets?
Reply 1: 1) It is 3D-only, if you test it you can see that the pattern piece doesn't change its dimensions in the 2D window. 2) & 3) No, it is not possible to save a preset. You will have to edit the shrinkage back to 100% or have two versions next to each other, one with shrinkage applied and the other one without.

Comment 6: I watched thisYouTube Series completely by taking notes.I don't remember that I got the answer of this question. Maybe I missed.So can you answer me please? Thanks.
Reply 1: Hi, click on the desired pattern pieces and then edit shrinkage in the Property Editor here:
content_description: "Learn how to accurately calculate and add the shrinkage ratio to your fabric to ensure precise measurements and optimal results in your sewing projects."

title: .ZFAB saving issues
content:
Hello, Clo

I've noticed this for a while now, but it really pissed me off today.

I have a huge amount of custom PBR fabrics that I create for a client. If I make any changes to the texture maps, say changing the texture format from .png to .jpeg, Clo saves the .ZFAB fabric along with the old .png. This increases the size of the fabrics significantly, making the models take longer to load.

![7b2ab639e07042af8b2e704004a7edee](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202508/d3f93968487842a8b34cd7cf07e6d492/images/7b2ab639e07042af8b2e704004a7edeeimage.png)

Deleting .pngs directly from the archive and editing .json cause file's error and CLO to crush.

So could you fix that?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you. Sent

Comment 2: Hi Michael, I have contacted tech support over this and will get back to you ASAP.
Reply 1: Hi Michael, development says this is not how ZFABs are supposed to work and have checked to make sure everything is going as should, it is not occuring for them. Could you share one of your affected ZFAB files with us so we can run tests on them? Please also share the current version of CLO you are on (visible on the bottom left of the CLO window). You can share the files here https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/d3f93968487842a8b34cd7cf07e6d492 and note that you are coming from the forums, so that the ticket is rooted to me. Thank you 🙂
content_description: This web page aims to address the issue of Clo retaining outdated texture maps, resulting in unnecessarily large fabric files that hinder model loading times, and to seek a solution for optimizing file management.

title: FEATURE IDEA: concerning the new trim improvements
content:
FEATURE IDEA: let user define closed state of Trims like slider buttons and add an export for special types of button trims. The trim exported saves the two pieces plus the closed state. So users can also create custom formed buttons. User adds the trim in closed state, CLO3D then takes the objects as trim parts, no matter how many and closed state is saved, open state loosens all objects individually, that way even complex trims with several loose parts work. Right click on one object of the trim opens a menu that allows to select open or closed state.

Same way you could work with fabric and trims like buckles, user selects vertices to attach to a trim, creates the closed state between fabric vertices and trims like buckles and saves everything, when selecting the buckle trim he can say closed and trims like buckles snaps to vertices in saved manner

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, thank you for this suggestion! We will pass it on as a feature request 🙂
Reply 1: ❤️
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive overview of a feature that allows users to define and export customizable closed states for button trims and buckles in CLO3D, facilitating the creation of intricate designs with precise control over trim functionality.
